description.narrative: Burundi is implementing a national Mpox management response project, involving the Ministry of Health, UNICEF, and other international partners like the pandemic fund. The project focuses on strengthening surveillance, laboratory capacity, healthcare workforce training, and community engagement to manage the outbreak and prepare for future health emergencies. Key activities include revising response plans, training health workers, strengthening diagnostic capabilities, providing psychosocial support, and engaging community volunteers through organizations like the Burundi red cross. Key Players and Commitments are: Ministry of Health: Africa CDC (Provided technical support, helped assess the national response through an Intra-Action Review (IAR), and intensified support in affected districts), UNICEF (Developed a multisectoral response plan to support affected communities, particularly children, focusing on case management, nutrition, WASH, and child protection), The Pandemic Fund (Partnering with Burundi to enhance national capacities in prevention, preparedness, and response to health emergencies, including strengthening surveillance and laboratory systems., WHO & IFRC ( Collaborating with health authorities to strengthen response pillars, train front-line responders, and engage community volunteers. ) Burundi have approved national Mpox and preparedness plan and Mpox level 3 ( Burundi Mpox Level 3 Emergency-2024-2025-01-13 Purpose of the project This project intends to intervene in the prevention of Mpox in the communities, the focus of will be for project participants to have a better world. This project will be implemented by 1 Outcome Outcome 1: Water, sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Under this outcome, we will implement 2 outputs: Output 1: 1000 hand wash items will be distributed to families to help control transmission at household level, Output 2: 1000 liquid Soaps bar distributed to communities, office of local administration Output 3: Capacity Building: training of 300 community health workers on hygiene and case referral mechanisms
